description:
## Outcome

The Mix release builder creates the macOS ARM64 package directory and deterministic archive with application code, a private OTP runtime, runtime data, launcher, license files, and metadata. It preserves fast dispatch and paint-first startup.

## Work

1. Implement the Mix release method confirmed by `jido_cli-tqg.7.14`.
2. Build the exact archive layout and name in the artifact contract.
3. Include `llm_db`, `req_llm`, `time_zone_info`, `extractous_ex`, and all required runtime resources without broken `priv` links.
4. Make `bin/jido` resolve paths relative to itself and invoke only the private runtime.
5. Enter the CLI before application startup. Do not put a release `eval` expression in the public launcher.
6. Preserve fast help and version, paint-first TUI, arguments, streams, terminal control, signals, and exit status.
7. Pin OTP, Elixir, package, and native dependency inputs.
8. Normalize archive ordering, timestamps, ownership, and permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The macOS ARM64 archive builds from source.
- [ ] The archive validates and can move after extraction.
- [ ] No system OTP is required.
- [ ] TUI, `run`, and `eval` start from the package.
- [ ] Help and version return before runtime startup.
- [ ] The first TUI frame appears before runtime-ready state.
- [ ] All required `priv` files and native libraries load.
- [ ] The archive layout can be installed by a later Homebrew formula.
- [ ] Repeated controlled builds have matching content or a recorded variance.

## Tests

Run builder unit checks, archive validation, and focused startup checks on macOS ARM64.

## Non-goals

Do not build another target, publish, sign, or create a Homebrew formula.
title: Implement the macOS ARM64 private-OTP artifact builder
